mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 3.8% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 3.8% in a month, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in core inflation (CPIAUCSL) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a weakening consumer demand environment that reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL and RSAFS decline in prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both CPIAUCSL and RSAFS decline in the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth exceeds 110 (index 2017=100), it signals robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO exceeds 110, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 2.0% in a single month, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over the past month indicates strong consumer spending that supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where RSAFS increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%), the labor market is tight, leading to higher wage growth and consumer spending, which boosts corporate earnings and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE is below 3.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and core inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate a monetary policy response to inflation, which increases real interest rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increase in prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increase in the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.
